record.context_brief: dominant maps from very general complete intersections
record.original_question: Let a and b be positive integers with a + b > 5, let S ⊂ P^4 be a very general smooth complete intersection of type (a, b), and let f: S → X be a dominant rational map of degree at least 2. Must the surface X be rational?

evidence.quote: (13.3) Let a and b positive integers such that a + b > 5 ... Let f : S → X be a dominant rational map of degree  2. Is the surface X necessarily rational?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers with $a+b>5$, and let $S \subset \mathbb{P}^4$ be a very general smooth complete intersection of type $(a,b)$ (i.e., the transverse intersection of two very general hypersurfaces of degrees $a$ and $b$). Suppose $f \colon S \dashrightarrow X$ is a dominant rational map of degree at least $2$ onto a smooth projective surface $X$. Must $X$ be rational?
artifact.status_search_result: A brief web search located related work by Bastianelli and collaborators on measures of irrationality and dominant rational maps from very general complete intersection surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^4$, but no source was found that conclusively settles the specific question of whether the target $X$ must be rational under the stated hypotheses. The status appears to be unresolved in the located literature.

status_evidence.title: Curves on complete intersections and measures of irrationality
status_evidence.snippet: measures of irrationality on very general codimension two complete intersections... confirming cases of a conjecture of Bastianelli, De Poi, Ein, Lazarsfeld, and Ullery
status_evidence.claim: Related conjectures on irrationality of very general complete intersections remain only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: On dominant rational maps from products of curves to surfaces of general type
status_evidence.snippet: existence of generically finite dominant rational maps from products of curves to surfaces of general type
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses dominant rational maps but not the specific rationality question stated.
